The European Union has 24 official languages. They are: Bulgarian, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hungarian, Irish, Italian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Maltese, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish and Swedish.

A few notes: the number has stood at 24 since Croatian was added when Croatia joined in July 2013. English remains an official language even after Brexit, because it is also an official language of Ireland and Malta (though Ireland nominated Irish and Malta nominated Maltese). Irish had a derogation limiting the amount of material translated into it, but that was fully phased out on 1 January 2022, so it now has full official-language status. Spain has requested official status for Catalan, Basque and Galician, but as of my knowledge that has not been approved (it requires unanimity in the Council).

The European Union currently has 24 official languages. Nadal drew level with Federer at 20 by winning the 2020 French Open, and both were later passed by Djokovic.

Japan's total fertility rate (TFR) in 2022 was 1.26, according to the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's Vital Statistics. This was a record low at the time (down from 1.30 in 2021), and it came alongside a record-low number of births — about 770,747 Japanese births in 2022, the first time the annual total fell below 800,000. (The record was subsequently broken again, with the TFR falling to about 1.20 in 2023 and 1.15 in 2024.)

35 states. The Equal Rights Amendment, passed by Congress in March 1972, was ratified by 30 states in its first year, but momentum slowed; Indiana became the 35th and final state to ratify before the original deadline, on 18 January 1977. No further states ratified between then and the 22 March 1979 deadline, leaving the total three short of the 38 (three-fourths of the states) needed for adoption. Note that five of those states — Nebraska, Tennessee, Idaho, Kentucky and South Dakota — had voted to rescind their ratifications by that point, though the legal validity of such rescissions is disputed. Congress subsequently extended the deadline to 30 June 1982, during which no additional states ratified.

35 states. Congress sent the ERA to the states on 22 March 1972 with a seven-year ratification deadline of 22 March 1979. By that date 35 of the required 38 states (three-fourths of the 50 states) had ratified it — leaving it three short. (Complicating matters, five of those states — Nebraska, Tennessee, Idaho, Kentucky and South Dakota — had passed measures purporting to rescind their ratifications, though the validity of such rescissions is legally disputed.) Congress subsequently extended the deadline to 30 June 1982, but no additional states ratified during the extension; Nevada (2017), Illinois (2018) and Virginia (2020) ratified long afterward, raising the total to 38, though the legal effect of those late ratifications remains contested.

According to the archaeological survey published by China's State Administration of Cultural Heritage in June 2012, the Great Wall — counting all sections built across all dynasties (Qin, Han, Ming and others) and including walls, trenches, natural defensive barriers, and associated structures such as beacon towers, fortresses and passes — has a total length of 21,196.18 kilometres (about 13,170 miles). This figure superseded the 2009 preliminary result of 8,851.8 km, which covered only the Ming dynasty wall.
